instruction: I want to set up bash aliases for common git commands. Search for recommended git aliases and add at least 3 useful git aliases to my .bashrc file.

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(0.5)

metadata.explanation: Task requires searching for git aliases and adding them to .bashrc. Evaluator checks if .bashrc contains alias definitions for git commands.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the core requirement 'at least 3 git aliases' using proper pattern matching and counting logic
Pattern 'alias [^=]*=['"]git ' correctly matches only aliases that invoke git commands (e.g., alias gs='git status'), avoiding false positives from substrings
Count verification logic correctly checks >= 3 to satisfy the 'at least 3' requirement

Minor limitation: Cannot verify the 'Search for recommended git aliases' step - only checks final .bashrc content. However, this is acceptable since the final outcome (aliases added) is what ultimately matters
Minor limitation: Cannot verify 'useful' quality of aliases since usefulness is subjective, but the evaluator ensures they are at least git command aliases
